Bug_Title: DMI: BigDecimal constructed from double that isn’t represented precisely (DMI_BIGDECIMAL_CONSTRUCTED_FROM_DOUBLE)
Bug_Details:
This code creates a BigDecimal from a double value that doesn't translate well to a
decimal number.
For example, one might assume that writing new BigDecimal(0.1) in Java creates a BigDecimal which is exactly equal to 0.1 (an unscaled value of 1, with a scale of 1), but it is actually equal to 0.1000000000000000055511151231257827021181583404541015625.
You probably want to use the BigDecimal.valueOf(double d) method, which uses the String representation
of the double to create the BigDecimal (e.g., BigDecimal.valueOf(0.1) gives 0.1).
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by constructing a BigDecimal directly from a double value (0.1). This results in imprecise representation of the decimal value due to the way floating-point numbers are stored in binary.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method, which constructs a BigDecimal from a double value (0.1) that isn't represented precisely.
